transcript.content: Hello, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in today?

I guess what finally made me come in is… I don’t feel like myself. The part of me that used to want to reach out to people, or enjoy my work, yoga, going to galleries, even journaling—it’s all gotten really quiet. I’m still doing what I have to do, but it feels like I’m mostly just moving through obligations.
How long have you been feeling this way—weeks, months, or longer?

It’s been months—about eight months now. It started around the time we took my older relative into our apartment, and since then this change in how I think, work, and connect with people has just kind of stayed.
Since this started about eight months ago, have you noticed any changes in your sleep—such as trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been tracking it closely. I don’t think there’s been a big change, at least not one that stands out to me.
Over these past eight months, have you noticed a change in your energy level—do you feel unusually tired or drained most days, even when you haven't done much?

I’m not sure I’d call it unusually tired. I don’t think my energy has changed in a really obvious way. Some days I feel worn down, but it’s hard to tell if that’s energy or just everything feeling harder lately.
Over these past eight months, would you say you feel down, sad, or empty most of the day, nearly every day?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve been stressed and not myself, but I wouldn’t say I feel sad or empty most of the day nearly every day.
Would you say you've lost interest or pleasure in almost all your usual activities nearly every day, most of the day, over these past eight months?

Yeah... I think that’s probably the biggest thing. I haven’t completely stopped doing things, but the part of me that used to look forward to people, my work, yoga, going to galleries, even journaling—it’s like that’s gotten really quiet. Mostly I’m just getting through what I have to do.
Over these past eight months, have you noticed trouble concentrating, focusing on tasks, or making everyday decisions more than usual?
I’m not really sure. I wouldn’t say I’ve noticed a major change with concentration or decisions. Maybe I’m slower with some things, but it hasn’t stood out to me as a separate problem.
Over these past eight months, have you noticed any significant change in your appetite or your weight, either an increase or a decrease, without trying?
Not really. My appetite’s been about the same, and I haven’t noticed any big weight change that I wasn’t trying for.

Do you notice that this loss of interest and enjoyment gets better on days when things are calmer with your relative's care, or does it stay pretty much the same no matter what's happening with that situation?

It stays pretty much the same, I think. Even when things are calmer, I don’t really bounce back into wanting to see people or enjoy work or yoga or galleries. I’m mostly just going through what I have to do.
Over these past eight months, have you found yourself feeling unusually worthless, guilty, or overly critical of yourself?
No, I don’t think so. I can be hard on myself sometimes, but not in a way that feels unusual or constant. I haven’t been feeling worthless or overwhelmed with guilt.
Over these past eight months, have you had any thoughts of death, dying, or that you'd be better off not being here?
No, I haven’t had thoughts like that. I haven’t been thinking about death or feeling like I’d be better off not being here.

Has this loss of interest affected your ability to perform your job duties or maintain your relationships, or are you still managing those areas about as well as before, just without the same enjoyment?

I’m still showing up to work, but I’m not doing as well as before. I’ve missed some grant deadlines, and my supervisor has quietly shifted a few of my more demanding clients to other clinicians. So… I’m managing on the surface, but I’m not really functioning at my usual level.

Like I said, I’m still going to work, but I’m not keeping up the way I used to. I’ve missed some grant deadlines, and my supervisor has moved some of my more demanding clients to other clinicians. So I’m functioning, but not at my normal level.

I know I already mentioned it, but yes—it has affected my work. I’m still showing up, but I’ve missed grant deadlines, and my supervisor has quietly moved some of my more demanding clients to other clinicians. So I’m getting by, but I’m not functioning at the level I usually do.
Aside from the loss of interest, would you describe your overall mood most days as low, down, or discouraged, even if 'sad' doesn't feel like the right word?
I’m not sure I’d call it low most days. It’s more like… flat, I guess. I don’t feel especially happy or excited, but I don’t always feel sad either. Just kind of dulled out.
Besides feeling flat or dulled, do you ever find yourself feeling hopeless, tearful, or discouraged about how things are going?

Not really hopeless, no. I mean, I get frustrated and kind of discouraged that I’m not on top of things like I usually am, but I wouldn’t say I’m breaking down crying or feeling like there’s no point. It’s more that flat feeling I mentioned.

inference.note: Symptoms remain tied to an identifiable, ongoing stressor (relative's caregiving) with persistent anhedonia/flat mood and functional impairment at work, but do not meet full criteria for MDD (no significant sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, guilt, or suicidal changes, and mood is not pervasively sad/hopeless). final_diagnosis.reason: The patient developed marked anhedonia and functional impairment (missed deadlines, reassigned clients) within months of a clear, identifiable psychosocial stressor (taking on caregiving duties for an older relative living in the home). Symptoms are disproportionate to the stressor and cause impairment, but full major depressive episode criteria are not met—no pervasive depressed/sad mood most days, no sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, guilt, or suicidal symptoms. Mood is described as 'flat/dulled' rather than sad or hopeless, and symptoms track with the ongoing stressor rather than being autonomous. This pattern—stressor-related, subsyndromal depressive symptoms with functional impairment—best fits Adjustment Disorder with depressed mood rather than Major Depressive Disorder.
